default_accounts_removed_or_changed.title: Default Accounts Removed or Changed
default_accounts_removed_or_changed.description: Shared-vocabulary attestation that the broker's shipped default accounts (e.g. RabbitMQ guest:guest) have been deleted or had their default credentials changed. False means a well-known default account remains usable, an immediate anonymous/default-credential foothold.

default_guest_remotely_reachable.title: Default Guest Account Remotely Reachable
default_guest_remotely_reachable.description: Interpreted boolean: the RabbitMQ built-in 'guest' user is present with its default password AND not restricted to loopback (loopback_users = none in rabbitmq.conf), so guest:guest can connect from remote networks. True is the insecure default-allow posture; the secure form deletes guest or sets loopback_users = guest.

anonymous_access_allowed.title: Anonymous Access Allowed
anonymous_access_allowed.description: Interpreted boolean derived from the broker auth configuration: clients can connect without credentials — e.g. RabbitMQ advertises the ANONYMOUS SASL mechanism in auth_mechanisms (rabbitmq.conf), or a Kafka listener accepts unauthenticated connections. True is insecure; the secure form restricts auth_mechanisms to PLAIN/AMQPLAIN/EXTERNAL (no ANONYMOUS).

kafka_authorizer_enabled.title: Kafka Authorizer Enabled
kafka_authorizer_enabled.description: Interpreted boolean: a Kafka authorizer is configured (authorizer.class.name set, e.g. org.apache.kafka.metadata.authorizer.StandardAuthorizer in server.properties) so topic/group ACLs are actually enforced. False means no authorization at all — any authenticated or anonymous principal has full access. Secure value is true.

kafka_allow_everyone_if_no_acl_found.title: Kafka allow.everyone.if.no.acl.found
kafka_allow_everyone_if_no_acl_found.description: The Kafka allow.everyone.if.no.acl.found flag (server.properties). True makes any resource without an explicit ACL world-accessible (default-allow), which Confluent strongly discourages in production; a deleted/misconfigured ACL silently opens access. Secure value is false.

least_privilege_access_enforced.title: Least-Privilege Access Enforced
least_privilege_access_enforced.description: Shared workspace attribute: whether broker principals are scoped to least-privilege rights (RabbitMQ per-vhost configure/write/read regexes scoped per role — producers write-only, consumers read-only — rather than '.*' on all three; Kafka explicit per-principal/per-topic ACLs rather than super-user or default-allow). False means application principals hold broad/wildcard rights, so any authenticated client can publish, consume, or reconfigure any queue/topic and a compromised low-privilege producer becomes a confused deputy.

wildcard_acls_used.title: Wildcard ACLs Used
wildcard_acls_used.description: Interpreted boolean: whether any application principal is granted wildcard authorization — RabbitMQ set_permissions with configure/write/read all '.*' (full access across the vhost), or Kafka ACLs using resource/operation wildcards (or a wildcard-equivalent super-user grant). The assessor reads the raw permission regexes / ACL list (rabbitmqctl list_user_permissions, kafka-acls --list) and sets this true if a non-admin principal effectively has all-resource rights. Modelled as an interpreted boolean rather than regex-matching the raw '.*' string, since the secure scoped regexes can themselves legitimately contain '.*' fragments (e.g. 'app\..*'), which would false-fire a substring match. True fires the exposure.

per_topic_acls_enforced.title: Per-Topic ACLs Enforced
per_topic_acls_enforced.description: Interpreted boolean: whether per-topic/per-queue authorization is actually enforced — Kafka has authorizer.class.name set (StandardAuthorizer) with allow.everyone.if.no.acl.found = false AND explicit per-principal/per-topic ACLs present; RabbitMQ has scoped per-vhost permissions rather than a single broad grant. False means there is effectively no per-topic least-privilege boundary (no authorizer, default-allow, or a flat permission model), so any authenticated client reaches every topic/queue. False fires the exposure.

flow_tls_encrypted.title: Transport TLS Encrypted
flow_tls_encrypted.description: Whether broker transport (AMQP, Kafka client and inter-broker channels) runs over TLS rather than cleartext. INSECURE when false: a plaintext listener is reachable — RabbitMQ listeners.tcp on 5672 with no ssl_options, or Kafka listeners = PLAINTEXT://:9092 / security.inter.broker.protocol = PLAINTEXT — exposing credentials and message payloads to network sniffing and MITM modification. Secure value: true (AMQPS 5671 / Kafka SSL:// or SASL_SSL:// listeners and SSL/SASL_SSL inter-broker protocol).

tls_only_transport.title: TLS-Only Transport
tls_only_transport.description: Whether the broker accepts ONLY TLS-protected connections, with no externally reachable cleartext listener remaining alongside the TLS one. INSECURE when false: a plaintext AMQP 5672 / Kafka PLAINTEXT 9092 listener is still reachable even though a TLS listener exists, so an attacker (or a misconfigured client) can be downgraded onto the cleartext port for sniffing/MITM. Secure value: true (plaintext listeners disabled or firewalled to trusted networks; only AMQPS/SSL/SASL_SSL reachable).

weak_tls_versions_enabled.title: Weak TLS Versions Enabled
weak_tls_versions_enabled.description: Interpreted flag: whether the broker's TLS listener still permits legacy TLS versions (TLSv1.0 / TLSv1.1) in addition to or instead of TLSv1.2/1.3. Derived from the raw protocol-version directive (RabbitMQ ssl_options.versions, Kafka ssl.enabled.protocols) rather than substring-matched, since a hardened value (TLSv1.2,TLSv1.3) excludes the weak versions but a raw match would false-fire. INSECURE when true: legacy TLS enables downgrade/MITM against the transport. Secure value: false (only TLSv1.2/TLSv1.3 negotiable).

server_certificate_validated.title: Server Certificate Validated
server_certificate_validated.description: Whether peer/certificate verification is enforced on the TLS connection (RabbitMQ ssl_options.verify = verify_peer; Kafka clients validate the broker via configured truststore). INSECURE when false: verify_none accepts any presented certificate, so an active attacker can terminate TLS with a forged certificate and perform a MITM even when 'TLS' is nominally enabled. Secure value: true (verify_peer / truststore-validated certificate chain).

service_to_service_mtls_enforced.title: Service-to-Service mTLS Enforced
service_to_service_mtls_enforced.description: Whether mutual TLS is enforced so the broker requires a client certificate and rejects certless/anonymous TLS clients (RabbitMQ ssl_options.fail_if_no_peer_cert = true with verify_peer; Kafka ssl.client.auth = required). INSECURE when false: fail_if_no_peer_cert = false or ssl.client.auth = none lets an unauthenticated peer establish a connection, weakening the channel's resistance to impersonation/MITM on the inter-service path. Secure value: true (mTLS required, certless clients rejected).

data_store_publicly_routable.title: Broker Listeners Publicly Routable
data_store_publicly_routable.description: Shared workspace attestation: the broker's data/messaging listeners (AMQP 5672/5671, Kafka 9092/9093, ActiveMQ OpenWire 61616) are bound to a publicly routable interface (0.0.0.0) and reachable from the internet rather than confined to a private/management network. True when the broker's listener is internet-reachable — a direct surface for credential abuse and known-CVE exploitation. Verify with 'ss -tlnp' that ports are bound to 127.0.0.1 / a private address and firewalled to trusted CIDRs.

management_ui_internet_exposed.title: Management UI Internet-Exposed
management_ui_internet_exposed.description: The broker's administrative management plane — RabbitMQ management plugin HTTP API/UI on 15672 (15671 TLS), or an equivalent admin console — is listening on 0.0.0.0 and reachable from the internet. True when the management UI is internet-exposed, a high-value admin-takeover surface. Secure posture binds management.tcp.port to a private interface / firewalls it to trusted CIDRs so it is not publicly routable.

segment_boundary_enforced.title: Segment Boundary Enforced
segment_boundary_enforced.description: Shared workspace attestation: network segmentation confines the broker so it accepts connections only from a management/trusted network (enforced in both broker config and network policy / firewall / security group). True when a segment boundary is enforced around the broker. When false, no segmentation isolates the broker and exposed listeners are reachable from untrusted networks — the exposure fires.

control_plane_api_not_publicly_exposed.title: Control-Plane API Not Publicly Exposed
control_plane_api_not_publicly_exposed.description: Shared workspace attestation: the broker's control-plane / admin API surface (RabbitMQ HTTP management API, Kafka admin/inter-node control, ActiveMQ console) is NOT publicly exposed — it is confined to a private/management network. True when the control-plane API is private. When false, the control-plane API is publicly exposed, giving attackers a direct administrative surface and the exposure fires (inter-node 25672 and management API must not be internet-reachable).

message_integrity_protected.title: Message Integrity Protected
message_integrity_protected.description: Interpreted boolean: whether messages carry per-message integrity protection (application-layer digital signature or MAC over the message body). Brokers do not sign message bodies natively (RabbitMQ/Kafka/ActiveMQ), so integrity must be enforced at the application layer — the assessor confirms producers sign and consumers verify a signature/MAC before acting on a payload. False means an attacker who can publish or modify in-flight messages can inject forged content that consumers cannot distinguish from legitimate traffic. Fires (exposure) when integrity is NOT protected.

producer_authentication_required.title: Producer Authentication Required
producer_authentication_required.description: Interpreted boolean: whether the broker requires authenticated producers before accepting a publish (no anonymous/guest write path). The assessor confirms there is no unauthenticated publish route — e.g. RabbitMQ guest deleted/loopback-only and ANONYMOUS removed from auth_mechanisms; Kafka has no reachable PLAINTEXT listener and an authorizer is configured. False means an attacker can connect with no credentials and inject messages directly into a queue/topic. Fires (exposure) when producers are NOT required to authenticate.

wildcard_publish_authorization.title: Wildcard Publish Authorization
wildcard_publish_authorization.description: Interpreted boolean: whether application principals hold wildcard/full publish authorization rather than scoped least-privilege write access. The assessor interprets the real authorization config — RabbitMQ per-vhost configure/write/read regexes all set to '.*' (full access), or Kafka allow.everyone.if.no.acl.found = true / no authorizer.class.name (default-allow). Modeled as an interpreted boolean to avoid the substring/has_element polarity trap on the raw regex/ACL values. True means any (or every) authenticated principal can write to any queue/topic, enabling forged-message injection even where authentication exists. Fires (exposure) when publish authorization is wildcard rather than scoped.

consumer_idempotency_or_dedup_enforced.title: Consumer Idempotency or Dedup Enforced
consumer_idempotency_or_dedup_enforced.description: Attested true when message consumers enforce idempotency or deduplication (e.g. dedup on a unique message/business key, broker-level dedup such as Kafka enable.idempotence/transactional producers, or an application-side processed-id store) so that re-delivering or re-submitting a previously processed message produces no duplicate side-effect. False (the firing state) means a captured legitimate message can be replayed to trigger duplicate side-effects (repeated payments, repeated commands). This is an application-layer property the assessor verifies about the consumer; the broker does not provide it natively.

message_freshness_nonce_bound.title: Message Freshness Nonce-Bound
message_freshness_nonce_bound.description: Attested true when messages carry an anti-replay binding the consumer validates — a per-message nonce, a monotonic sequence number, or a signed timestamp enforced against a freshness/acceptance window — so a stale captured message is rejected on resubmission. False (the firing state) means messages carry no nonce/sequence/freshness binding, so previously captured legitimate messages remain indefinitely re-playable. Verified at the application/protocol layer, not a broker config knob.

encrypted_at_rest.title: Encrypted at Rest
encrypted_at_rest.description: Whether the broker's persisted message store (Kafka log.dirs segments, RabbitMQ mnesia/quorum-queue data) sits on a volume encrypted at rest (LUKS or cloud KMS/EBS, AES-256). Brokers do not encrypt message bodies natively, so cleartext PII/secrets in message bodies persist on disk when this is false. Maps to the dossier config key broker_at_rest_encryption; insecure when the data directory is on an unencrypted disk.

retention_schedule_enforced.title: Retention Schedule Enforced
retention_schedule_enforced.description: Whether messages carry a bounded TTL/retention so sensitive payloads are not retained indefinitely (Kafka retention.ms/retention.bytes set to a finite value, not -1; RabbitMQ x-message-ttl / message-ttl policy). False when retention is unbounded, allowing cleartext PII/secrets to accumulate on disk and leak into backups or readable storage. Maps to the dossier config key message_payload_sensitivity_and_ttl.

secrets_masked_in_logs.title: Secrets Masked in Logs
secrets_masked_in_logs.description: Whether sensitive message payload fields (PII, credentials, tokens) are masked/redacted before message bodies are written to broker logs or persisted diagnostics. False when payloads leak verbatim into local logs, compounding the at-rest exposure on an unencrypted volume.

queue_length_limit_enforced.title: Queue Length Limit Enforced
queue_length_limit_enforced.description: Interpreted: a per-queue maximum length / overflow bound is enforced on the broker (RabbitMQ max-length / x-max-length-bytes / overflow policy with a dead-letter exchange, or Kafka retention.bytes per topic) so an unbounded queue cannot grow until memory/disk is exhausted. False (no queue-length cap, default unbounded) lets a producer or attacker flood the queue and deny service. Assessor verifies via 'rabbitmqctl list_policies' (max-length present) or 'kafka-configs --describe' (finite retention.bytes).

memory_disk_watermark_configured.title: Memory/Disk Watermark Configured
memory_disk_watermark_configured.description: Interpreted: broker memory/disk safety watermarks are configured to back-pressure or block publishers before resources are exhausted (RabbitMQ vm_memory_high_watermark and disk_free_limit set in rabbitmq.conf; Kafka log retention/quota equivalents). False (default unbounded memory, no disk_free_limit) means a flood drives the broker to OOM / disk-full and a denial of service. Assessor verifies via 'grep -E vm_memory_high_watermark|disk_free_limit rabbitmq.conf'.

rate_limiting_or_lockout_enabled.title: Rate Limiting or Lockout Enabled
rate_limiting_or_lockout_enabled.description: Shared-vocabulary interpreted boolean: per-client connection/publish rate limiting or producer quotas are enforced (RabbitMQ per-connection/channel limits and credit flow, Kafka client producer quotas) so a single principal cannot saturate the broker. False means no producer quota — an abusive or compromised producer can issue unbounded connections/messages and exhaust capacity.

ddos_protection_in_place.title: DDoS Protection in Place
ddos_protection_in_place.description: Shared-vocabulary interpreted boolean: network/connection-level flood protection guards the broker's reachable listeners (connection limits, SYN/connection rate caps, upstream load-balancer or WAF/scrubbing, IP-based throttling) so a volumetric or connection-exhaustion flood is absorbed before it reaches broker queues. False means the broker's listeners are directly exposed to flooding with no protective layer.

unpatched_known_rce_cve.title: Unpatched Known RCE CVE
unpatched_known_rce_cve.description: Interpreted: the broker software is running a release affected by a known, publicly-exploited remote code execution CVE (e.g. ActiveMQ OpenWire deserialization RCE, CVE-2023-46604 — fixed in ActiveMQ Classic >= 5.15.16/5.16.7/5.17.6/5.18.3 or Artemis >= 2.31.2). The assessor compares the deployed broker version (activemq --version / image tag) against the advisory fixed releases and sets this true when the running build is below the patched version. True fires this exposure; a fully patched broker is false.

edge_appliance_patched_within_sla.title: Broker Patched Within SLA
edge_appliance_patched_within_sla.description: Shared workspace attestation: the network-reachable broker software (the edge/appliance surface) is kept current with security patches within the organisation's remediation SLA. Secure value is true (patches applied within SLA); false means the broker is behind on security updates and exposed to known-CVE exploitation — which fires this exposure. Reused across vectors to express the patch-currency posture of internet- or network-facing components.

native_deserialization_of_untrusted_data.title: Native Deserialization of Untrusted Data
native_deserialization_of_untrusted_data.description: Interpreted: the broker transport (e.g. ActiveMQ's OpenWire marshaller) deserializes attacker-influenced serialized class types from untrusted/unauthenticated network clients without a class allow-list, allowing instantiation of arbitrary classpath classes and shell-command execution. True fires this exposure (the deserialization sink is reachable and unrestricted); a broker that restricts deserialization to a safe allow-list or does not expose native deserialization to untrusted peers is false.

access_audit_trail_enabled.title: Access Audit Trail Enabled
access_audit_trail_enabled.description: Whether the broker records an access/authentication audit trail (connection and auth attempts on AMQP/Kafka listeners). Shared workspace attribute. Insecure (false) when the broker runs default local-only logging with no connection/auth audit — anonymous access and credential abuse are then undetectable. Maps to broker_audit_logging in the component dossier (RabbitMQ auth/connection event logging; Kafka authorizer.logger).

security_events_fully_logged.title: Security Events Fully Logged
security_events_fully_logged.description: Whether all security-relevant broker events are captured — including publish/consume operations and authorization (ACL) decisions, not just startup/error logs. Shared workspace attribute. Insecure (false) when message tampering and abuse via publish/consume leave no forensic trail. Kafka logs ACL decisions via the authorizer logger; RabbitMQ logs auth/connection events.

logs_stored_on_separate_system.title: Logs Stored on Separate System
logs_stored_on_separate_system.description: Whether broker logs are shipped off-box to a separate system / SIEM rather than retained only on the broker host. Shared workspace attribute. Insecure (false) when logging is default local-only with no off-box shipping, so an attacker who compromises the broker can erase the trail (T1562.008) and there is no durable forensic record.

broker_admin_events_audited.title: Broker Admin Events Audited
broker_admin_events_audited.description: Whether broker administrative changes are audited — RabbitMQ vhost/user/permission (ACL) changes via rabbitmqctl, Kafka ACL/super.users/topic-config changes. Insecure (false) when admin events are not logged, so privilege escalation and silent ACL loosening on the queue go unrecorded. Secondary trigger specific to the admin-event facet of this vector.
